question: A 25-year-old previously healthy woman presents to her PCP reporting cessation of menses for the past 6 months. Previously, her period occurred regularly, every 30 days. She also complains of decreased peripheral vision, most noticeably when she is driving her car. She denies any recent sexual activity and a pregnancy test is negative. Upon further work-up, what other physical findings may be discovered?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Cessation of menses for 6 months" -> "Possible hormonal imbalance" -> "Increased risk of decreased bone density" -> 80% CHAIN: "Decreased peripheral vision" -> "Possible pituitary gland involvement" -> "Enlarged thyroid may be discovered on physical examination" -> 80%
enhanced_information: The presentation of a 25-year-old woman with cessation of menses for 6 months and decreased peripheral vision suggests a possible hormonal imbalance and pituitary gland involvement. Further work-up may reveal an enlarged thyroid, indicating potential pituitary gland dysfunction. Breast mass, decreased bone density, and renal failure are less likely based on the clinical presentation.
